messages:
alex (PM): Heads-up: we need to lock down launch criteria for the "Predictive Burst Autoscale" initiative. Major cross-team deps: runtime batching, infra autoscale policy, and security review for on-prem fallback. Can we align on must-have vs nice-to-have by EOD?

maya (Eng): I can take runtime answers. must-have for us: deterministic KV-cache eviction policy, API for prefetch hints, and a canary rollout plan. nice-to-have: adaptive batch sizing in first release.

sam_r (Runtime): +1 on deterministic eviction. Also need to decide acceptable tail-latency target when autoscale is in cooldown. Proposal: 300ms p95 for interactive routes, 800ms p95 for batch async. Thoughts?

priya (Infra): Those SLOs look OK but autoscale warm-up requires reserved GPU slots for bursts or we miss cooldown targets. We need to know burst frequency and budget (RU/month). Can product commit a target for peak qps and expected burst shape?

alex (PM): We have customer asks: 1) retail partner expects spikes ~5x baseline for ~2-5 mins, 2) analytics jobs can be batched off-peak. For launch: commit to supporting 3x sustained and 5x short bursts. Budget TBD — we need finance input but want infra to assume baseline.

maya (Eng): If 5x short bursts are required, runtime needs a fast-path: prefix cache warm-up + prefetch API. I can spec the API today. Will that change infra requirements?

priya (Infra): Yes, prefetch helps but we still need reserved burst pool or fast GPU spin-up. Two options: reserved fractional capacity (cheaper predictability) or cold-start optimization (cheaper but riskier). Which do we prioritize?

dmitri (Security): We must include threat model for prefetch and cache warming if customer data is used. For on-prem/private deployments, prefetch should respect tenant isolation and KMS access patterns. Also need a Security Design Review before canary.

alex (PM): OK — tradeoffs decision: reserved burst pool for hosted and a best-effort cold-start for private deployments. We can mark private as "no SLA for burst" at launch. That narrows infra work.

sam_r (Runtime): Implementation notes: I'll add a `prefetch_hint` field to the request schema and a `warm_priority` signal in internal routing. Sample config snippet:
```
route_config: 
  burst_pool: true
  prefetch_hint: boolean
  warm_priority: low|medium|high
```
This will let infra route to reserved GPUs when set.

maya (Eng): Will add `prefetch_hint` and doc for fallback semantics. Also need a test harness for spike simulation — can opsbot run synthetic bursts?

opsbot: @maya I can schedule synthetic load jobs. Use tag `pb-autoscale-test`. Next available slot: tomorrow 09:00 PT.

priya (Infra): Action items: 1) I'll draft infra plan for reserved burst pool and cost estimate, 2) define autoscale cooldowns and slot reservation semantics. Expect PR by Tue EOD.

dmitri (Security): Action: I'll start the Security Design Review checklist and tag in the CSPM and KMS owners. Target review in 3 business days.

alex (PM): Great. From product side: I'll firm the launch criteria: 1) runtime implements prefetch + deterministic eviction, 2) infra provides reserved burst pool for hosted with cost estimate, 3) security signoff complete, 4) canary run with synthetic bursts with opsbot and perf within agreed SLOs. If any item slips, we gate full GA and ship limited beta (hosted only) instead.

maya (Eng): Noted. I'll push runtime PRs today and link to this thread.

sam_r (Runtime): I'll prototype warm_priority routing and run local spike tests.

priya (Infra): Will ping finance for budget input and include in PR.

alex (PM): Thanks all — I'll consolidate these action items into a single doc and post OKR-linked ticket. If anyone objects to the tradeoffs above, speak now or DM. :thumbsup:

maya (Eng): :thumbsup:

sam_r (Runtime): :thumbsup:

priya (Infra): :thumbsup:
